hook: Write this down. One sentence. It will do more for your discipline than any morning routine.
topic: The Personal Standard / Pre-Written Decision Rules
body:
**Write a single sentence that describes the minimum standard you hold for yourself. Not the ideal. The minimum.**

Not "I will be highly productive every day." That is a preference. It has no edge.

Something like this: "I do not skip the morning workout regardless of how I slept." Or: "I do not open my phone before 8am." One behaviour. One line. No flexibility clause.

This is not a goal. A goal is something you aim for. A standard is something you enforce. The distinction matters because a goal permits negotiation — you can be making progress and still below it. A standard is binary. You held it or you didn't.

When the resistance arrives tomorrow morning — and it will, it is predictable — your brain will begin constructing a reason. A reasonable one. The standard is your pre-written response to that reason. Not a new decision made under pressure. A decision made in advance, in a clear state, that is simply being executed.

Write one line tonight. Not a list. One line. The thing you most reliably negotiate yourself out of. Make it a standard, not a preference. And tomorrow, you will have a reference point that was not there before.

A reference point changes the conversation. The download is in my bio — it walks you through the full framework.
